mof_ops.detail: MoF June 2026 supply: two regular sale auctions - 17 Jun (settle 19 Jun) PLN 6,000-12,000m and 24 Jun (settle 26 Jun) 6,000-12,000m, each in OK0129 / NZ0331 / PS0731 / DS0436 / NZ0936 'plus possible IZ and other series' (total 12-24bn); final offer 2 days before each auction; additional sale after each auction at the minimum accepted price. ONE switch auction: 3 Jun (settlement 8 Jun, after the 4 Jun holiday) - sold: OK0129 / NZ0331 / PS0731 / DS0436 / NZ0936 + possible IZ/other; bought back: DS0726 (outstanding 33,192m), PS1026 (26,370m), WZ1126 (18,753m), OK0127 (16,019m), PS0527 (32,830m). NO T-bill auctions planned in June. Retail offer for June unchanged in rates: OTS0926 2.00%, ROR0627 4.00% (ref+0.00), DOR0628 4.15% (ref+0.15), TOS0629 4.40%, COI0630 4.75% (CPI+1.50), EDO0636 5.35% (CPI+2.00), ROS0632 5.00%, ROD0638 5.60% (first periods). Deputy FM Jurand Drop (comment to the plan, PAP 15:07): budget accounts to exceed PLN 200bn at end-May (187.7bn at end-April). MoF (PAP 15:08): 2026 gross borrowing needs ~56% financed.

mof_ops.detail: No sale auction and no T-bill auction in the windows (29 May-14 Jun). June plan (29 May): sales on 17 and 24 Jun (offers due 15 and 22 Jun - outside), 'Przetargi sprzedazy bonow skarbowych nie sa planowane'. MoF DB: no wholesale bond row between the 27 May sale and the 3 Jun switch, none 4-16 Jun; T-bill DB: no row between 8 May and July (later rows exist, not used). PKO (PAP 8 Jun 09:49): a short-term absence of new primary supply supports POLGBs.

Financing of 2026 gross borrowing needs: ~56% (MoF communique 29 May, PAP 15:08; was ~54% on 25 May and >50% of domestic SPW per Millennium 28 May). No newer ratio after the 3 Jun switch in the windows. Budget accounts: Drop (29 May 15:07) expected >PLN 200bn at end-May; MoF monthly report (PAP 8 Jun 11:29): PLN 208.3bn at end-May, the highest since at least Jan 2025 (187.7bn end-April). MoF report (Skrot 8 Jun 17:02): 2026 debt still to be redeemed (as of 31 May) PLN 148.7bn; public-sector liquidity consolidation 150.5bn (term deposits 71.2bn, O/N 79.3bn); average maturity of domestic debt 4.11Y (4.15Y end-April), total 5.70Y (5.79Y); 'MF do konca roku przekaze na rynek 132 mld zl' (payments to the market by year-end, as reported). Drop (PAP 10 Jun 12:47): POLSTR-linked SPW outstanding PLN 40bn as of 8 Jun, with 'large, normal demand' for POLSTR floaters. Budget execution after May NOT published in the windows (MoF 'operational' data after April only: capital spending 13.9bn = 19.1% of plan; mining tax 2.5bn = 78.2%, Skrot 10 Jun 17:02). Last known deficit: 89.3bn after April (15 May).

MoF: non-resident holdings of domestic SPW rose PLN 0.6bn in April to 190.5bn (share 12.1% from 12.2%; 11.8% end-2025). Domestic SPW debt +25.2bn to 1,576.2bn; banks incl. NBP +19.4bn to 825.4bn (52.4%), domestic non-banks +5.2bn to 560.3bn (35.5%) (PAP 15:11). SPW secondary-market turnover in April -15.9% m/m to PLN 2,045.2bn (Skrot 17:06).

MoF: EU funds inflow in April EUR 1.06bn (cohesion 537.9m, CAP 434.37m), YTD 10.33bn; Poland paid in 776.8m in April, YTD 3.14bn (PAP 13:39). EC (Skrot 29 May 17:06): ~EUR 6.6bn SAFE advance paid to Poland. KPO: PLN 31bn tranche received (Pelczynska-Nalecz, Skrot 2 Jun 17:02; two more tranches this year); EC: KPO paid EUR 34.15bn by 2 Jun (62% of allocation, of which 19.7bn loans; Skrot 3 Jun 17:01); ECOFIN approved changes to Poland's KPO on 12 Jun, so the next payment request can be sent (Skrot 12 Jun 17:08). Citi (Skrot 1 Jun): MoF FX conversions Jan-Apr ~EUR 7.3bn, ~80% possibly at the NBP.

facts.text: PKO Dziennik 29 May: expects May flash CPI at 3.7% y/y (= consensus), above the 3.5% upper band on fuel prices; on 28 May POLGBs moved 0/+3bp with the 10Y at 5.79%; a confirmed US-Iran memorandum could push EUR/PLN toward 4.22-4.195 and extend falls in POLGB yields.

Erste Codziennik 29 May: forecasts May CPI at 3.7% (from 3.2%); EC ESI for Poland rose 0.9pt to 100.1 in May (third-highest in 24 months), consumer inflation expectations fell back below 25pt from a 33.3pt April peak.

Millennium daily 29 May: forecasts May CPI at 3.7% y/y, slightly above the band; a print above 3.5% need not trigger an automatic MPC reaction given weaker wage growth; expects continued wait-and-see.

PAP FX/FI morning: PAP consensus for May flash CPI 3.7% y/y, 0.2% m/m (April 3.2% / 0.6%); Pekao: a breach of the band would be a 'cezura' for the NBP but no hasty reaction expected; PKO: a durable US-Iran deal would favour further normalisation of POLGB yields.

GUS flash: May CPI 3.1% y/y, -0.3% m/m vs PAP consensus 3.7% / +0.2%; food and non-alcoholic beverages 0.5% y/y (-1.0% m/m), energy 5.0% y/y (0.0% m/m), fuels 12.3% y/y (-0.1% m/m). Final May CPI due 15 Jun.

CPI reactions: the surprise came mainly from food (-1.0% m/m). PKO: core ~3.0-3.1%, hike expectations 'exaggerated', CPN mitigates the energy shock, no second-round effects; Alior: core ~3.0% from 3.1%, supports stable rates; Bank Pocztowy (Kurtek): core 2.5-2.9%, lower risk of breaching the band; mBank: June CPI similar, July could start with a 2.

Erste revised its 2026 CPI path down: inflation increasingly likely to stay near 3% all year (assuming CPN through end-2026 and Brent gradually below $90), which could reduce the MPC's inclination to consider hikes; upside risks to food prices from drought and frosts.
MoF: EU funds inflow April EUR 1.06bn, YTD 10.33bn; contributions 776.8m (YTD 3.14bn). EC: ~EUR 6.6bn SAFE advance paid to Poland (Skrot 17:06).

June supply plan (gov.pl 29 May; PAP 15:07-17:06): sales 17 Jun and 24 Jun (PLN 6-12bn each), one switch on 3 Jun (buyback DS0726/PS1026/WZ1126/OK0127/PS0527), no T-bills; Drop: budget accounts >PLN 200bn at end-May (187.7bn end-April); MoF: ~56% of 2026 gross needs financed.

facts.text: MoF: non-residents added PLN 0.6bn of domestic SPW in April to 190.5bn (12.1% share); banks incl. NBP +19.4bn to 825.4bn (52.4%); SPW secondary turnover -15.9% m/m to 2,045.2bn (Skrot).

Fiscal items (Skrot 17:06): the windfall-tax bill's impact assessment puts revenue at ~PLN 5bn for Mar-Dec 2026 (Orlen tax base ~4bn); VAT gap fell to 4.9% in 2025 from 7.9%; Sejm sent an alcohol-excise bill (+15% in 2026, +10% in 2027, for the NFZ) to committee; MoF: unchanged excise rates mean a falling excise/GDP ratio (2.4% in 2025).

Fuel package: the energy ministry says CPN extension decisions will be taken every two weeks (geopolitics too volatile to decide for the whole summer); maximum prices Pb95 6.05, ON 6.34 zl/l for 30 May-1 Jun. The VAT/excise cuts currently run to 15 Jun (extended 28 May).
BGK plans an FPC switch tender on 18 Jun: buys back FPC0427, may sell FPC0229/FPC0231/FPC0332/FPC0235; BGK may also issue abroad in Q2.

PAP FX/FI close: POLGB yields fell ~20bp along the curve after the CPI miss (16:55: WS0428 4.39%, PS0731 5.16%, DS0436 5.60% vs 4.55/5.34/5.77% in the morning); EUR/PLN 4.2277. Millennium (Chrapek): yields back at early-May levels, further falls possible early next week, then consolidation.
Weekend: 29 SAFE contracts worth PLN 78bn signed on Saturday 30 May (Kosiniak-Kamysz, 'record'); ~290m invoices issued in KSeF by 26 May (MoF).

PAP week ahead: MPC decision Tue 2 Jun (afternoon), Glapinski conference Wed 3 Jun 15:00; PAP survey: reference rate held at 3.75% until Q3 2027, -25bp at end-2027; GS: hold to Q1 2027; Pekao: hike talk can be shelved after May CPI. Q1 GDP details Mon 09:30 (PAP consensus: consumption 3.9%, investment 3.0%, domestic demand 3.8%); PMI Mon 09:00; MoF switch offer Mon 15:00, switch Wed 12:00; Thu 4 Jun holiday; Fri 5 Jun 14:00 reserves and May minutes.
PKO Dziennik 1 Jun: on 29 May POLGB yields fell 17-25bp, 10Y -17bp to 5.62%; forecasts PMI 48.6 (consensus 48.5); deal-driven de-escalation supported the week's rally.

Millennium daily 1 Jun: the CPI miss cut yields ~16bp on 29 May; on the June plan - with few maturities, net issuance will be high, which may pressure ASW spreads; the >200bn of budget cash allows flexible debt management.

Erste Codziennik 1 Jun: the CPI miss sharply cut priced NBP hikes - FRAs dated 6M+ fell ~20bp, IRS -15-16bp, bonds -14-18bp with ~4bp steepening. S&P's Vartapetov told PAP the key downgrade trigger would be a weaker medium-term growth outlook; no significant downgrade risk from the fiscal position alone (debt moderate, good structure).

facts.text: GUS: Q1 GDP 3.5% y/y (flash 3.4%), 0.6% q/q (flash 0.5%); Q4 4.1%. Private consumption 3.3% (consensus 3.9%), investment 2.4% (3.0%), domestic demand 3.7% (3.8%).

GDP comments: growth was driven almost entirely by consumption (mBank: investment added only 0.3pp; still sees ~7% investment growth in 2026 from Q2); Port: weaker consumption outlook, falling wage growth; Middle East the main risk.
S&P Global manufacturing PMI May 49.4 (April 48.8) vs consensus 48.5 (PKO 48.6, Erste/Millennium 48.3); economists: industry copes relatively well with the supply shock.
MoF switch offer for 3 Jun: sells OK0129, NZ0331, PS0731, DS1034, DS0436, NZ0936; buys back DS0726, PS1026, WZ1126, OK0127, PS0527.
facts.time_basis: MoF slot 15:00; PAP Skrot 17:02 = upper bound

facts.text: Domanski (EKF Sopot): MoF wants to stabilise and strengthen public finances step by step and return to projects raising NFZ revenue; sustaining fast growth is key; the economy shows above-average resilience. S&P's Vartapetov: Poland's rating could be higher with fiscal consolidation and better governance assessment.

Local governments posted a Q1 surplus of PLN 44.7bn vs a planned 47.2bn deficit (MoF); OFE moved 1.331bn to ZUS (slider); windfall-tax draft: first advance due 25 Aug for Mar-Jul; MoF proposes raising the PCC exemption to 3k zl; KUKE expansion to add PLN 10bn of financing (MoF, 10:58).

PAP FX/FI close: POLGB yields rose on renewed US-Iran risk (16:45: WS0428 4.44%, PS0731 5.25%, DS0436 5.70%); EUR/PLN 4.2375. PKO (Marek): pressure should ease - 2Y below 4.40% and 10Y below 5.60% possible by week-end; the MPC and Glapinski should curb 2026 hike pricing.

PKO Dziennik 2 Jun: on 1 Jun POLGB yields rose 8-13bp with global trends; market pricing fully includes a 25bp NBP hike in October and about half of another by year-end; expects the MPC/Glapinski to reinforce that there is no room for hikes in 2026; 2Y below 4.40% and 10Y below 5.65% by week-end.

Millennium daily 2 Jun: hold expected (consensus); markets still price 1-2 hikes this year; the MPC has room to stay wait-and-see and keep rates stable to end-2026. On 1 Jun swaps rose ~10bp, 10Y ~5.73%.

PAP FX/FI morning: ING - after May CPI the market cut 2026 hike pricing to about +25bp; ING expects Glapinski to keep cautious rhetoric and the market to keep one hike priced, limiting room for lower yields; Pekao: 10Y +~10bp on Monday, chance of a correction.

EKF consensus (17 teams, forecasts to 22 May): GDP 3.5% (2026), 3.0% (2027); CPI 3.3% / 3.1%, at 2.5% target in 2028-29; NBP rate flat at 3.75% with a slightly higher chance of one 25bp cut in 2027-29. GG deficit 6.9% of GDP (2026), 6.4% (2027), 5.8%, 5.3%; EU debt ~66% (2026), ~70% (2027), ~75% (2029).

MPC (1-2 Jun) held: reference 3.75%, lombard 4.25%, deposit 3.25%, rediscount 3.80%, discount 3.85% - as expected. Statement (16:00): May CPI 3.1% eased mainly on food; hold given geopolitical uncertainty; further decisions depend on incoming data on inflation and activity; risk factors unchanged (fiscal policy, fuel-price regulation, activity, wages); FX intervention possible.

MRPiPS will recommend a 2027 minimum wage of PLN 4,986 (+3.7%) and 32.60 zl/hour (50% of the forecast 2027 average wage of 9,971); unions want >=5,200; the government must present its proposal to the RDS by 15 Jun.

MPC reactions: Millennium - statement unchanged in key parts, no mention of low core (est. -0.1/0.0% m/m), base case no change at least to end-2026; ING - the CPI drop gives the MPC more time, base case stable rates in 2026; PKO - hikes not necessary if CPI stays in the band; Pekao - stable rates at least to end-2026, good chance in 2027 too; BPS - external risks could still sway a majority to hike.
NBP: banking-sector net profit Jan-Apr 2026 PLN 13.22bn (-19.9% y/y); interest income -10.3%, interest costs -21.9%, impairments -23.8%.

Fiscal Council chair Dudek: consolidation must combine revenue and spending measures; before the next election there is no room for tax cuts (incl. PIT threshold indexation) or new benefits. IMF office (Krogulski): a rising debt path makes Poland vulnerable; it needs fiscal space. Digital-tax draft in inter-ministerial consultation (Gawkowski).
BGK priced FPC bonds in EUR: 8-year EUR 1.25bn and 15-year EUR 750m, demand EUR 4.6bn.

EBRD cut Poland's GDP forecasts to 3.5% (2026) and 2.8% (2027), both -0.2pp; growth supported by maximum KPO absorption before the August 2026 deadline and defence spending rising to 4.8% of GDP; SAFE funds channelled via the armed-forces fund.
MSiG: Tyrowicz voted against the April MPC resolution approving the NBP 2025 financial statements; 9 members in favour; Maslowska did not vote.
PKO Dziennik 3 Jun: on 2 Jun POLGB yields moved -4/+3bp, 10Y -4bp to 5.69%; favourable CPI is a key argument for the hold amid Middle East uncertainty.

Millennium daily 3 Jun: expects Glapinski to keep wait-and-see, saying fundamentals give room to keep rates stable; the decision was a formality given falling CPI and lower inflation expectations; base case no change at least to end-2026, with escalation the main hike risk; the switch auction should have limited market impact.
Erste Codziennik 3 Jun: after the MPC hold, IRS and FRAs dated 9M+ fell 4-5bp on 2 Jun; EUR/PLN stable.

PAP FX/FI morning: PLN weaker at 4.24/EUR, POLGB yields up a few bp (09:17: WS0428 4.47%, PS0731 5.24%, DS0436 5.69%); Millennium: pressure on yields possible until Glapinski, who may sound 'relatively non-hawkish'; PKO expects sideways trade.

OECD Economic Outlook: Poland GDP 3.0% (2026), 2.6% (2027); CPI 3.7% / 2.7%; recommends postponing further rate cuts to Q2 2027; GG deficit 6.9% / 6.3% of GDP; debt to exceed 60% and keep rising; calls for better-targeted energy support.

Glapinski (conference 3 Jun 15:00): May CPI below expectations reduces the probability of a hike; the MPC authorised him to say the current rate level is good - high enough to stabilise inflation, no reason to change or discuss it; a durable oil rise plus the end of government fuel-price support would trigger an immediate hike debate (likely a majority for a hike); shock smaller than feared, wage growth slowing; real rate +0.6%; gold ~613t (~324bn zl).

PAP FX/FI close: POLGB yields fell from morning levels after Glapinski (16:17: WS0428 4.42%, PS0731 5.24%, DS0436 5.67%), PLN slightly weaker (EUR/PLN 4.2407). Noble: hikes shift further out; Erste (Luzinski): rates unchanged in coming months, CPI near 3% to year-end if CPN stays and Brent falls below $90.

EC European Semester (3 Jun): recommends continuing to correct the excessive deficit while allowing defence spending, more efficient spending and a broader tax base; the EC will treat member states' high-energy-price spending leniently under EU fiscal rules (a clause added to the defence escape clause). KPO: EUR 34.15bn paid to Poland by 2 Jun (62%).
Goldman Sachs: Glapinski was much more dovish than in May (reversal driven by the large May CPI miss); the bar for hikes stays high; forecasts no change until Q1 2027 unless oil rises further.
SKRM to discuss the 2027 minimum wage and 2027 macro indicators on 8 Jun (originally 3 Jun).
Thu 4 Jun (Corpus Christi): no Polish session; the PAP holiday digest carries no Polish macro or debt news; no NBP average-rate table appeared in the PAP feed that day (last: 106/A on 3 Jun).
Eurostat: Polish retail sales April -0.1% y/y, -1.5% m/m.
PKO Dziennik 5 Jun: this week POLGB yields rose ~6-12bp (2Y 4.47%, 10Y ~5.70%) vs Bunds +8-13bp; the 2Y outperformed on Wednesday as Glapinski cooled hike expectations.

Millennium daily 5 Jun: market rates rose ~8bp on 3 Jun until Glapinski, then fell 3-4bp; 10Y ~5.72%; his dovish tone (slower wages, high real rates) argued against the ~1 hike by year-end and ~2 within 12 months the market had priced.

Erste Codziennik 5 Jun: Glapinski said the shock was milder than expected and low May CPI reduced hike odds; Erste expects unchanged rates in coming months; drought threatens crops - an upside risk for food prices.
PAP FX/FI morning: thin post-holiday market following core markets and US payrolls (consensus +88k, 4.3%); EUR/PLN opened at 4.2350.
NBP: official reserve assets rose to EUR 255.60bn in May (254.80bn); monetary gold USD 89.09bn.

May MPC minutes (5-6 May): the CPI outlook is highly uncertain even short term and hinges on fuel prices (Middle East) and the shape and duration of fiscal-regulatory fuel measures; a further CPI rise possible in coming months; some members: core should stay within the band; shock much smaller than in 2022, demand not excessive, labour market less tight; some flagged a risk of renewed wage pressure; most saw the hold as justified.
PAP FX/FI afternoon: PLN flat near 4.23/EUR; POLGB yields +2-4bp vs the morning (14:25: WS0428 4.46%, PS0731 5.27%, DS0436 5.71%).

Draft amendment to the nuclear special act: the 2026 budget limit for state support to PEJ cut to PLN 8bn from 11bn, 2030 raised to 9.6bn from 6.6bn; max fuel prices Pb95 6.00, ON 6.48 zl/l for 6-8 Jun.

PAP week ahead: a thin domestic calendar - April balance of payments Fri 12 Jun 14:00 (Erste: C/A deficit >EUR 1bn on costlier commodity imports, a PLN negative); SKRM on the 2027 minimum wage and macro indicators; MoF PDP Wed 10 Jun 15:00. Erste: a 3.7% minimum-wage rise would not raise inflation concerns.
PKO Dziennik 8 Jun ('Hawkish NFP'): first June week brought global risk-off, a stronger USD and higher yields on Fed hike pricing; USD/PLN tested 3.68.
Erste Codziennik 8 Jun: strong US May labour data; the stronger dollar weakened PLN and POLGB yields rose.

PAP FX/FI morning: PLN 4.25/EUR, POLGB yields up by over 10bp (09:33: WS0428 4.58%, PS0731 5.40%, DS0436 5.84%). PKO: a rebound likely - 2Y below 4.45%, 10Y below 5.7% - backed by softer MPC rhetoric, solid domestic demand and no new primary supply in the short term; Millennium: higher oil may lift yields slightly.

Credit Agricole kept GDP forecasts at 3.3% (2026) and 3.0% (2027); cut CPI to 2.8% (2026) but 3.8% in 2027; Q1 investment (2.4%) the main disappointment; Olipra: food inflation to pick up in coming quarters.
MoF: retail bond sales May PLN 5,398.5m (April 5,609.1m), ROR 42%, COI 18%; YTD 30.2bn (-0.6bn y/y).

MoF monthly report: budget accounts PLN 208.3bn at end-May (highest since at least Jan 2025; 187.7bn end-April). Skrot 17:02: 2026 redemptions still due (as of 31 May) 148.7bn; liquidity consolidation 150.5bn; average maturity domestic 4.11Y, total 5.70Y; 12M C/A deficit 0.8% of GDP after March.

PAP FX/FI afternoon: Millennium - the market still prices ~1-2 NBP hikes by year-end; base case stable rates; ~15bp room to the next resistance along the curve, 10Y resistance ~6.05% (14:06: WS0428 4.52%, PS0731 5.35%, DS0436 5.79%).

Fitch Ratings (June forecast round, not a rating action): Poland GDP 3.3% in 2026 (from 3.6%), 2.9% in 2027; end-2026 CPI 3.5% (3.3%); NBP at 3.75% to end-2026, one 25bp cut in 2027, 3.50% to end-2028; USD/PLN 3.65 at end-2026. Ratings: Moody's A2 negative, Fitch A- negative, S&P A- stable.

Eurostat: Poland's debt-service cost 4.5% in 2025, among the highest in the EU; 65.2% of cohesion 2021-27 funds contracted by 7 Jun; government to discuss 2027 wage, pension and macro parameters on Tue 9 Jun.
PKO Dziennik 9 Jun: on 8 Jun POLGB yields rose 1-13bp, 10Y +6bp to 5.87%, on Israel-Iran missile exchanges after strong US payrolls.
Erste Codziennik 9 Jun: the government reviews 2027 fiscal parameters today; the current gas tariff was extended to year-end; bond yields and market rates edged up.
PAP FX/FI morning: Alior - after Monday's +7-8bp, slight falls possible as oil eases; BGK - 10Y seen at 5.80-5.85%; PKO watches whether the government's 2026 CPI forecast changes from April's 2.5%.
EY: core CPI 3.0% in 2026 and 3.5% in 2027, NBP rates unchanged; GDP ~3.6% (2026), 2.8% (2027).
MRPiPS: registered unemployment May 5.9% (April 6.0%) vs PAP consensus 5.9%; 917.2k unemployed (-17.1k m/m, +134.3k y/y); vacancies -17% y/y.

Government 2027 macro forecasts (KPRM): GDP 3.1%, average CPI 2.5%, nominal wages 5.6%, employment ~11m FTE (in line with April's WZM, which assumed GDP 3.6% and CPI 2.5% in 2026, pre-war). Budget-sphere pay +3% in 2027; pensions indexation at least 3.48% (cost ~16.7bn) (Skrot 21:06).
MPC's Maslowska (Bloomberg): at the moment rate cuts are more likely than hikes.

VIG/C-Quadrat TFI: current POLGB yields relatively attractive, more room for a debt rally if geopolitics calm; May was the best month of 2026 so far for Polish treasuries. Erste: CEE8 GDP 2.3% in 2026 vs 2.7% expected before the Iran war.

PAP FX/FI close: POLGB yields fell 11-14bp vs ~3bp in core markets (17:14: WS0428 4.46%, PS0731 5.27%, DS0436 5.71%); Bank Pocztowy (Kurtek): dovish Glapinski plus low CPI make markets pull back NBP hike pricing.

PKO Dziennik 10 Jun: on 9 Jun POLGB yields fell 8-18bp, 10Y -13bp to 5.74%; the government plans a 2027 minimum wage of PLN 4,950 (+3.0%, as in 2026; MRPiPS had sought 3.7%) and 32.30 zl/hour, public pay +3%, pensions >=3.48%; parameters go to the RDS; MF's 2026 forecasts not yet presented.

facts.text: Detail on Maslowska's Bloomberg remarks (PKO, Erste 10 Jun): the May CPI drop is optimistic but not yet enough to consider easing; starting a cut debate would need CPI durably below 3.5% and no geopolitical deterioration; hikes cannot be fully excluded given instability; ending the CPN package could lift CPI above 4%.
facts.time_basis: PDF CreationDate (local, CEST) = upper bound (first dated mention of these details)

facts.text: Erste Codziennik 10 Jun ('Dovish signal from the MPC'): Maslowska sees better chances of cuts than hikes under strict conditions; on 9 Jun FRAs 3-6M fell ~10bp and 9-12M ~20bp; Erste's base case: no NBP change at least to end-2026.
Millennium daily 10 Jun: on 9 Jun swaps fell nearly 15bp and bonds similarly, partly on Maslowska's dovish remarks.
PAP FX/FI morning: PKO sees EUR/PLN ~4.245 ahead of US CPI; Millennium: a strong US CPI and the expected ECB hike could push core and Polish yields up.

Deputy FM Drop: WIBOR's end on 31 Dec 2036 (orderly wind-down, no new WIBOR contracts after 2026) is optimal and safe; MoF sees 'large, normal demand' for POLSTR floaters - POLSTR-linked SPW outstanding PLN 40bn as of 8 Jun.
MoF: PDP debt end-Q1 2026 PLN 2,008.2bn (+4.9% vs end-2025) = 50.6% of GDP; EDP debt 2,444.3bn = 61.6% of GDP (2025: 59.7%).

PKO cut its 2026 average CPI forecast to ~3.0% from 3.3% (May food fall of 1.0% m/m unprecedented this century; no second-round effects); the risk of breaching 3.5% is much lower; keeps the NBP on hold at least to end-2026, notes MPC voices on possible cuts while markets still price hikes.

MoF operational budget data after April: capital spending PLN 13.9bn (19.1% of plan), mining tax 2.5bn (78.2%); MoF analysing (not pursuing) a VAT cut on passenger transport. PIE MIK index +6.5pt to 101.0 in June. Windfall-tax bill on Thursday's SKRM agenda (21:02).

PAP FX/FI close: POLGB yields extended declines (16:51: WS0428 4.42%, PS0731 5.26%, DS0436 5.70%); ING (Sutowicz): partly Maslowska's remark that a cut is her base case, reinforcing Glapinski; US CPI 4.2% in line; ECB hike expected.

MPC's Dabrowski (Polsat News): after the fall in inflation there is no reason to hike for now; CPI should not leave the target band; if the supply shock passes and the global situation calms, there will even be room to cut.
PKO Dziennik 11 Jun: on 10 Jun POLGB yields moved 0/-4bp, 10Y unchanged at 5.74%; US CPI 4.2% y/y in line.
Erste Codziennik 11 Jun: Dabrowski - no reason to hike, room for cuts may appear; KPO spending April PLN 5.35bn, YTD 16.7bn; PLN weaker again, yields slightly lower.

PAP FX/FI morning: EUR/PLN marginally above 4.25 (3-week high); POLGB curve slightly lower; Millennium: Dabrowski's dovish remarks offset core-market pressure, and PLN 2.7bn of May inflows into domestic investment funds may stabilise debt in coming weeks.
World Bank kept Poland's GDP forecasts at 3.1% (2026) and 2.6% (2027); global growth cut to 2.5%.

Windfall-tax bill (new draft): rate cut to 60% from 75%; 2026 revenue cut to PLN 3.8bn from 4.75bn. Motyka: energy, state-assets and finance ministries still analysing, no decision yet on extending CPN. Domanski: working to lower energy prices for energy-intensive industry. FUS contribution coverage 81.5% in Q1.

PAP FX/FI close: EUR/PLN ~4.256, POLGB yields down again (16:55: WS0428 4.35%, PS0731 5.19%, DS0436 5.66%). PKO (Adamiak): the market expects fewer NBP hikes and MPC voices even hint at cuts, but very large borrowing needs and the deficit keep yields fairly high. ECB +25bp (unanimous), as expected.
PKO Dziennik 12 Jun: POLGB yields fell for another day on 11 Jun; until Tehran credibly confirms the US-Iran deal, volatility should stay limited with yields near Thursday's closes.
Erste Codziennik 12 Jun: Trump expects an Iran deal within days; ECB hiked 25bp and raised its inflation forecast; EUR/PLN rose to 4.255 while bond yields and market rates fell.
Millennium daily 12 Jun: forecasts the April C/A at EUR -550m (12M deficit ~0.8% of GDP), still a PLN-stabilising factor.
BIEC Future Inflation Index rose 1.8pt in June (fourth rise in a row); the inflation impulse is spreading, helped by commodity prices and higher long POLGB yields.
PAP FX/FI morning: PKO - credible signs Iran accepts the deal (immediate Hormuz opening) would push POLGB yields toward 4.20% (2Y), ~5% (5Y) and ~5.55% (10Y) in coming days; EUR/PLN ~4.25.

NBP: April current account EUR -1,558m vs PAP consensus -342m (PKO calendar consensus -505m); exports +6.6% y/y (consensus 5.9%), imports +7.8% (3.5%). ING (Kasek): 12M C/A deficit 0.9% of GDP (0.8% in March), driven by fuel imports.
facts.time_basis: exact NBP release 14:00; PAP Skrot 17:08 = upper bound

facts.text: MPC's Dabrowski (Bloomberg): a rate cut is now more likely than a hike; almost all MPC members are more optimistic on inflation and on the needed policy adjustment.

MoF regulation (Dz.U. 12 Jun) extends the reduced VAT on some fuels to end-June. Evening (Skrot 21:06, MoF-near source): the excise cut will not be extended - from 15 Jun only the VAT cut and the maximum price apply (statutory basis to 30 Jun). ECOFIN approved changes to Poland's KPO.
BGK (Dumicz to PAP Biznes): Q3 2026 issuance will focus mainly on prefunding the FPC's 2027 needs; ~30% of the targeted prefunding already secured.

PAP FX/FI close: EUR/PLN 4.243-4.256, POLGB yields lower vs the morning (17:50: WS0428 4.45%, PS0731 5.09%, DS0436 5.57%); XTB (Kwiecien): a US-Iran deal is not a done deal; prolonged stalemate would keep inflation pressures - negative for debt.
PM Tusk (13 Jun, Lomza): the government will end the CPN fuel-price project 'now, in summer'; good signals on ending the US-Iran conflict.
Weekend: PiS presented programme points incl. exiting ETS, exempting pensioners from tax and contributions up to PLN 2.5k and raising the second PIT threshold to PLN 180k.

The periodic change announced 27 May (R 2026-05-28, known; 'Portfele_obligacji_2026_05_27.pdf') took EFFECT on 29 May 2026 (after the session): DS0436 joins TBSP (18 -> 19 bonds) and B5Y; PS0527 leaves B1Y3Y (5 bonds), B1Y4Y (8) and B1Y5Y (11); NZ0331 and NZ0928 enter BWZ (9 bonds). Stats as of 26 May: TBSP YTM 4.97%, mod dur 3.68, value PLN 908.9bn; B1Y3Y 4.52% / 1.85 / 235.7bn; B1Y4Y 4.67% / 2.35 / 407.1bn. The 3 Jun switch (R 2026-06-05; settles 8 Jun) cuts PS0527 (a TBSP constituent) by 7,424m and adds to OK0129/PS0731/DS0436/DS1034 - units change only at the next periodic change. GPWB calendar: 4 Jun 'dzien bez sesji' (Corpus Christi); next bond-index announcement 26 Jun, periodic change 30 Jun (outside). Equity-index items (3 Jun, 12 Jun announcements) not relevant. NBP published no FX table on 4 Jun (106/A on 3 Jun; 107/A on 5 Jun, R 2026-06-08).

wz_coupons.note: No WZ, NZ or PP coupon/rate notice was published 29 May-14 Jun: the MoF 'komunikaty-dlug' list goes from the June plan (29 May) to a 15 Jun FX-account notice (outside, title only). Coupons in force: WZ1126-WZ0533 3.96% for 25 May-25 Nov 2026 (notice 20 May); WZ0330/WZ0930 3.86% for 25 Mar-25 Sep; PP0931 per the 19 Mar notice. The 3 Jun switch (R 2026-06-05) bought back 1,745.876m of WZ1126 (outstanding ~17.0bn after, derived).

digest.2026-06-01: 29-31 May: May flash CPI fell to 3.1% y/y (-0.3% m/m) vs 3.7% expected, as food dropped 1.0% m/m; economists see core near 3% and less pressure for hikes (Erste: CPI near 3% all year). POLGB yields fell ~20bp along the curve. MoF June plan: switch on 3 Jun, sales on 17 and 24 Jun (PLN 6-12bn each), no T-bills; ~56% of 2026 needs financed; budget accounts >200bn at end-May (Drop). BGK plans an FPC switch on 18 Jun.
digest.2026-06-02: 1 Jun: Q1 GDP revised to 3.5% y/y (flash 3.4), but consumption (3.3%) and investment (2.4%) missed forecasts; May PMI rose to 49.4 (48.5 expected). MoF offers OK0129, NZ0331, PS0731, DS1034, DS0436 and NZ0936 at the 3 Jun switch, buying back DS0726, PS1026, WZ1126, OK0127, PS0527. PAP survey: hold at 3.75% until Q3 2027. Yields rose on US-Iran setbacks; PKO sees the 10Y below 5.60% by week-end.
digest.2026-06-03: 2 Jun: The MPC held (ref 3.75%) as expected; the statement notes May CPI eased mainly on food and keeps decisions data-dependent, with risk factors unchanged. Banks keep a no-change base case for 2026; ING: hike pricing cooled to ~+25bp for 2026, PKO: an October hike is still fully priced. EKF consensus: GG deficit 6.9% of GDP in 2026, debt ~70% in 2027. MRPiPS proposes a 3.7% minimum-wage rise. BGK priced EUR 2bn of FPC bonds.
digest.2026-06-05: 3-4 Jun: Glapinski: lower May CPI cuts hike odds; rates are high enough, no reason to change or discuss them; a hike debate would come only with durably higher oil and the end of fuel support. GS, Noble and Erste read it as dovish; yields fell from the morning. MoF switch (MoF DB): PLN 11.63bn sold vs 10.90bn bought back (PS0527 7.42bn). OECD: CPI 3.7% in 2026, no cuts before Q2 2027. EC: leeway for energy spending. 4 Jun holiday.
digest.2026-06-08: 5-7 Jun: May MPC minutes: the CPI outlook is highly uncertain even short term and hinges on fuel prices and the fuel measures; a further CPI rise was possible; some members flagged wage risks; most backed the hold. Millennium: before Glapinski ~1 hike by year-end and ~2 in 12 months were priced. NBP reserves rose to EUR 255.6bn. POLGB yields rose ~6-12bp on the week (PKO) and edged up on Friday ahead of US payrolls.
digest.2026-06-09: 8 Jun: Budget accounts reached PLN 208.3bn at end-May; 148.7bn of 2026 redemptions remain. May retail bond sales were 5.40bn. Fitch's forecast round (no rating action): GDP 3.3% in 2026, NBP flat at 3.75% to year-end, one cut in 2027. Yields jumped 10bp+ in the morning on Middle East strain and Fed hike pricing; Millennium: 1-2 NBP hikes still priced by year-end; PKO expects a rebound. Week: PDP (Wed), April C/A (Fri).
digest.2026-06-10: 9 Jun: MPC's Maslowska (Bloomberg): cuts are now more likely than hikes, conditional on CPI staying below 3.5% and no escalation. The government's 2027 macro path: GDP 3.1%, CPI 2.5%, wages 5.6%; public pay +3%, pensions at least +3.48%. Registered unemployment 5.9% as expected. POLGB yields fell 11-14bp as NBP hike pricing receded (Kurtek). EY: rates unchanged, core 3.0% in 2026.
digest.2026-06-11: 10 Jun: MPC's Dabrowski: no reason to hike after the CPI fall; room even for cuts if the world calms. PKO cut its 2026 CPI forecast to ~3.0% and sees no hikes; Erste: FRAs 9-12M fell ~20bp on 9 Jun. The 2027 minimum wage was set at PLN 4,950 (+3.0%). PDP debt PLN 2,008.2bn (50.6% of GDP) at end-Q1, EDP 61.6%. Drop: POLSTR SPW PLN 40bn. Windfall-tax bill to the SKRM.
digest.2026-06-12: 11 Jun: POLGB yields fell again as the market priced fewer NBP hikes (PKO's Adamiak), though large borrowing needs keep yields high; EUR/PLN ~4.256. ECB +25bp as expected. Windfall-tax draft: rate cut to 60% from 75%, 2026 take PLN 3.8bn (from 4.75bn). Motyka: no decision yet on extending CPN. World Bank kept Poland's GDP at 3.1%/2.6%. Funds took in PLN 2.7bn in May (Millennium).
digest.2026-06-15: 12-14 Jun: April C/A deficit EUR 1.56bn vs ~0.34bn expected (fuel imports; 12M 0.9% of GDP, ING). Dabrowski (Bloomberg): a cut is now more likely than a hike; most MPC members more optimistic on inflation. The fuel VAT cut runs to 30 Jun but the excise cut ends (from 15 Jun); Tusk: CPN to end in summer. BGK: Q3 issuance to prefund 2027 FPC needs (~30% secured). PKO: an Iran deal could take the 10Y to ~5.55%.

mpc.gist: Hold: ref 3.75, lombard 4.25, deposit 3.25, rediscount 3.80, discount 3.85 (as expected). May CPI 3.1% eased mainly on food; hold amid geopolitical uncertainty; further decisions depend on inflation and activity prospects; risk factors unchanged (fiscal policy and fuel-price regulation, activity, wages); FX intervention possible.

Lower May CPI reduces the hike probability; on the MPC's authority: current rates are good, high enough, no reason to change or discuss them; a hike debate (likely majority) only if oil rises durably and fuel support ends; shock smaller than feared, wages slowing; real rate +0.6%; extraordinary meeting possible but not in the air; gold ~613t.
Voted against the April resolution approving the NBP 2025 financial statements (9 in favour; Maslowska did not vote). Not a rate vote.

CPI outlook highly uncertain even short term, driven by fuel prices and the fuel measures; further CPI rise possible; core seen in the band by some; shock smaller than 2022, demand not excessive; some flagged wage-pressure risk; most saw the hold as justified; data-dependent.
At the moment rate cuts are more likely than hikes (only this sentence is dated 9 Jun; PAP 10 Jun dates the interview to Monday 8 Jun, ING/Millennium to 9 Jun).
